headline: Acquisitions lift revenue, but costs pressure earnings
summary_short: EPR Properties' Q2 2026 revenue rose to $196M (+10.1% y/y, +8.2% q/q) on property acquisitions, rent escalators, and the Six Flags attraction-portfolio deal, while consolidated net income fell to $67M (-11.2% y/y) on higher interest expense and a retirement charge; FFOAA per diluted share still grew 12.7% y/y to $1.42.
summary_long: Revenue grew to $196M (+10.1% y/y) on $14.8M of net contribution from 2025-2026 acquisitions and developments (including the $304.4M Six Flags attraction-portfolio purchase) and $3.4M of escalations on existing leases. Operating income fell 3.9% y/y to $107M and net income fell 11.2% y/y to $67M, on higher interest expense (lower capitalized interest, higher average borrowings) and a new retirement/severance charge, partly offset by a $1.3M credit-loss benefit tied to converting a $70.0M mortgage note into an owned property. FFOAA per diluted share still rose 12.7% y/y to $1.42. Cash fell to $16M from $68M q/q on acquisition spending; long-term debt rose 17.9% y/y to $3,293M. Dividend held at $0.930/share, up from $0.885 y/y. This 10-Q contains no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: MD&A cites 2026/2025 investment and disposition activity, contractual rent/interest escalators, lower other income from fewer operating properties, and a new retirement/severance charge as the major factors shaping results.

Minimum rent rose $14.8M from 2025-2026 property acquisitions/developments (including the $304.4M Six Flags attraction deal) plus $3.4M from lease escalations, partly offset by $0.5M lost to dispositions.

Higher interest expense (less capitalized interest, more average borrowings) and a new retirement/severance charge outweighed revenue growth, partly offset by a swing to a credit-loss benefit from the mortgage-to-property conversion.
Tracks the net income decline; diluted share count also rose slightly (+0.6% y/y), adding a small further per-share drag.
Same net income decline as diluted EPS, with a similarly modest increase in basic share count year over year.
Revenue growth from acquisitions and rent escalators outpaced growth in property operating expenses, per the disclosed revenue and expense-line figures.
Higher depreciation and amortization from 2026/2025 acquisitions and developments, partly offset by dispositions, weighed on operating income despite revenue growth.
Revenue growth from acquisitions outpaced the rise in operating and G&A expense; management does not separately reason about EBITDA itself.
Interest expense, net rose on lower capitalized interest and higher average borrowings, partly offset by interest income on short-term investments, per management's own footnote.
Cash fell to $16.2M from $68.5M q/q, funding the $304.4M Six Flags acquisition and other 2026 investment spending; y/y it is still up from $13.0M on ATM equity proceeds.
Debt rose on increased average borrowings used to fund investment spending, including the Six Flags acquisition, per management's own interest-expense footnote.
